"Will drive the reimbursement infrastructure" names no body, no policy and no observable decision.
A necessity claim about a "robust new code set": no code, no body and no date. The "are coming" clause is background.
"Will need" complexity billing and longer monitoring: a necessity claim, not a decision by a payer or the FDA.
"Disastrous" is an evaluation of a hypothetical. No event and no threshold.
"An access barrier measured in years" has no named series, no payer and no countable set.
Buy-and-bill "likely to be necessary" sits inside a recommendation. No body issues a G or J code by a date.
"Expensive drugs" names no drug, no price and no series.
A price rise with no drug, no benchmark and no named price series.
No payer, no treatment and no coverage decision can be written from "will require economic data".
"Undercut financial support" and "limiting future innovation" have no threshold and no named series.
"Other payors follow Medicare" names no treatment, no policy and no payer that can be checked.
Team dispensing: no rule, no label and no measurable practice count.
A list of clinic requirements. No decision by a regulator or payer and no countable adoption.
"Large, vertically integrated organizations" is not a countable set and no company event is named.
"Set and setting are crucial" cannot be resolved on any source.
"More common place" consolidation: a comparative with no benchmark and no named series.
"Access will narrow" has no metric, no series and no threshold; the condition is also untestable.
An evaluation of a hypothetical FDA requirement, not a claim that the FDA adopts it.
A structural statement about the class. No regulator action, payer action or countable practice measure.
Denial of retail-pharmacy dispensing: the rebate-driven pharmacy-benefit model "it will not use". Same asset and outcome type as E-0067.
"The questions that will determine" names no event and no criterion.

event.asset: SNT (Stanford Neuromodulation Therapy) or another accelerated TMS protocol for bipolar depression
event.entity: Any sponsor of an accelerated TMS trial in bipolar depression
event.title: Accelerated TMS (SNT) trial in bipolar depression meets its primary endpoint
event.proposition: A randomized controlled trial of SNT or another accelerated TMS protocol in bipolar depression meets its prespecified primary efficacy endpoint.
event.criterion: TRUE on the date of the first sponsor topline release, ClinicalTrials.gov results posting or peer-reviewed publication, dated after the statement date, reporting a randomized controlled trial of SNT or another accelerated TMS protocol (more than one session per day) in bipolar depression whose prespecified primary efficacy endpoint met statistical significance. Open-label series and secondary endpoints do not count. FALSE at the deadline when no such result is reported.

resolution_source.name: ClinicalTrials.gov results posting; peer-reviewed publication or sponsor release

records.note: Efficacy call on bipolar depression. E-0006 is written on accelerated iTBS for depression, a different indication, so a new event.

event.entity: US health plans (commercial or public payers)
event.title: A US health plan covers intravenous ketamine for bipolar depression
event.proposition: A US health plan publishes a medical policy that covers intravenous ketamine as medically necessary for bipolar depression.
event.criterion: TRUE on the effective date of a published medical policy, coverage bulletin or fee schedule of a US health plan that lists intravenous ketamine as covered or medically necessary for bipolar depression (including treatment-resistant bipolar depression). Esketamine coverage, coverage for unipolar depression alone, case exceptions and trial-only payment do not count. FALSE at the deadline when no such policy has taken effect.

resolution_source.name: US health plan medical policy bulletins and fee schedules
